title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B series C months after $2.1B round
summary: Isomorphic Labs has raised a $5 billion series C round, marking the second time in six months that the AI drug development startup has pulled off a multibillion-dollar financing.

title: AriBio’s oral Alzheimer’s drug meets monotherapy goal in phase 3 as Fosun weighs licensing option
summary: AriBio’s erectile dysfunction med-turned Alzheimer’s disease candidate mirodenafil has delivered some mixed results from a global phase 3 trial. Fosun Pharma has an option to in-license the PDE5 inhibitor.

title: Sellas marks 9-month survival benefit in late-stage leukemia vaccine study
summary: Sellas Life Sciences’ cancer vaccine for acute myeloid leukemia has passed a phase 3 test with a more than nine-month improvement in overall survival.

title: Marrow extracts $120M series B to advance preclinical blood disease therapy
summary: A new biotech targeting blood disorders, aptly called Marrow Therapeutics, has launched with $173 million in combined funding and a preclinical lead program aimed at sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.

title: Lilly signs $5.9B deal with Stipple to unlock oncology targets
summary: Eli Lilly has struck a $5.9 billion deal to partner with Stipple Bio on oncology drug candidates that more precisely target tumor cells.

title: CG preps new, expanded bladder cancer plans with FDA after ph. 3 win
summary: CG Oncology showed in a late-stage study that its immunotherapy cretostimogene reduced the risk of tumor recurrence in certain patients with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer following surgery.

title: Helus' chemically modified psychedelic hits key goals in phase 3 depression trial
summary: Helus Pharma's oral chemically modified version of psilocybin hit the key goals of a phase 3 study as an adjunctive treatment in major depressive disorder.

title: Biogen inks $411M neurodegeneration pact with protein degrader biotech TrimTech
summary: Cambridge, U.K.-based TrimTech Therapeutics has linked up with Biogen in a collaboration worth up to $411 million in biobucks to develop protein degraders for neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Lilly secures another myelofibrosis option via $1.5B deal for JPM-founded Calytrix
summary: Eli Lilly has added another myelofibrosis prospect to its pipeline courtesy of a $1.5 billion deal for Massachusetts biotech Calytrix Bio.

title: J&J pays $2.2B upfront for Ollin to challenge Roche’s Vabysmo with phase 3 bispecific
summary: Johnson & Johnson has struck a deal to buy Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 billion upfront, establishing itself as a threat to Roche’s blockbuster eye disease drug Vabysmo.

title: Aclaris drops TSLP program from pipeline after flunking phase 2 eczema test
summary: A phase 2 study of Aclaris Therapeutics’ bosakitug in atopic dermatitis has missed its primary endpoint, adding to the setbacks anti-TSLP antibodies have encountered in the indication.

title: Building resilient biomanufacturing supply networks
summary: Global scale, regional proximity and harmonized quality systems can strengthen biologics supply resilience

title: Flagship commits £100M to set up AI-focused biotech incubation outpost in London
summary: Flagship Pioneering has picked London as the site of the venture capital powerhouse’s first company-creation unit outside of its hometown.

title: Big Pharma-backed Seawolf surfaces with $100M to hand, $1.2B Sanofi DNA med pact
summary: Seawolf Therapeutics has emerged from the deep with $100 million to fuel its DNA therapeutic ambitions and a billion-dollar deal with Sanofi.

title: Chinese scientists fired after child dies in gene editing study: report
summary: Chinese authorities have fired two researchers over their roles in the death of a child in a gene editing study, according to reports in Chinese state media.

title: Tandem Mobi sees FDA clearance for tubeless AID system
summary: Tandem Diabetes Care has picked up FDA clearance of its Tandem Mobi system, a tubeless automated insulin delivery device cleared for up to seven days of wear.

title: Sofinnova books biggest-ever $815M fund with an eye toward up-and-coming ‘global leaders’
summary: Life sciences venture capital firm Sofinnova Partners has closed its largest fund ever to the tune of $815 million backing around 15 clinical development companies mostly based in Europe.

title: FDA rejects Summit’s ivonescimab, derailing US arrival of much-hyped PD-1xVEGF class
summary: The FDA has issued a complete response letter to Summit Therapeutics, derailing the immediate U.S. launch of a drug class that many industry heavyweights believe could eventually dethrone Merck & Co.’s Keytruda.

title: Charles River pays $470M for 2 Frontage bioanalysis labs in Pennsylvania
summary: Charles River Laboratories has acquired Tigermed’s Frontage laboratory sites for $470 million upfront to advance its bioanalysis footprint.

title: The promise of molecular gates and what comes next
summary: Gate Bioscience is developing a new class of medicines designed to eliminate disease-causing proteins at their source. In this episode of "The Top Line," Gate co-founder and CEO Jordi Mata-Fink, Ph.D., discusses the promise of molecular gates, the biotech's expanded partnership with Eli Lilly and its plans to bring the technology into the clinic.

title: Rezolute gets an uplift from phase 3 tumor hyperinsulinism win ahead of FDA meeting
summary: A phase 3 clinical trial of Rezolute’s ersodetug in tumor hyperinsulinism has hit its primary endpoint, boosting the biotech ahead of a potential filing for FDA approval in another indication.

title: Cellectis will shed 70% of workforce as part of in vivo pivot
summary: Cellectis’ pivot from allogeneic CAR-Ts to in vivo therapies is set to come at the expense of 70% of its workforce.

title: ‘They’ve been misdiagnosed for too long’: Researchers use 10-protein panel to improve ALS detection
summary: By the time a neurodegenerative condition has been diagnosed, it's often too late. At the point of detection, the disease may already be causing irreversible damage, fueling an urgent search for ways to identify biological clues earlier and track their progression.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Bristol Myers' research chief out amid R&D reorganization
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's research chief is departing as the company restructures R&D. Summit Therapeutics cut ties with multiple launch team members, including its CCO, ahead of a high-stakes FDA decision. And OncoNano appointed its interim chief, a former FDA commissioner, to the permanent CEO spot.

title: Microglia mediate motor memory decay through activity-dependent phagocytosis of myelin sheaths
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02505-8Hu et al. showed that motor memory decay involves microglia engulfing memory-related myelin sheaths. Reduced engram activity lowers CD47, a ‘don’t eat me’ signal, thus promoting microglia-mediated myelin clearance and facilitating memory decay.

title: Distinct prelimbic microcircuits control sensory and affective dimensions of neuropathic pain
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02498-4Gan et al. report the cellular mechanisms underlying dysbalance of prefrontal brain activity in mice with neuropathic pain and delineate the circuitry through which the prefrontal cortex exerts top-down control of sensory and emotional aspects of pain.

title: Enhancer-targeted CRISPR-A rescues haploinsufficiency and mutant phenotypes in organoid models of autism
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02504-9CRISPR activation targeted to enhancers of autism risk genes CHD8 and SCN2A selectively increased expression and reversed mutant phenotypes in both patient-derived and gene-edited neuron and cortical organoid models of autism.

title: Gene discovery and pleiotropic architecture of multidimensional pain in a genome-wide association study of >1.2 million individuals
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02455-1We conducted a meta-analytic genome-wide association study of multidimensional pain in >1.2 million European-ancestry individuals. We identified 343 independent loci, which, alongside findings from a sex-stratified GWAS and other analyses, expand our knowledge of the genetics of pain.

title: Sour Tastes Hijack the Tongue to Mute Sweetness, Bitterness, and Saltiness
summary: Why does a sour bite overpower sweet, salty, and bitter flavors? A new study reveals that taste buds act as miniature processing hubs, releasing serotonin in response to sourness to mute competing flavors before signals ever reach the brain.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, neurobiology, serotonin, SfN, sour taste, taste, taste perception

title: Older Brains Lose Synchronization Between Movement and Body Temperature
summary: Even when 24-hour circadian rhythms persist into old age, faster multi-hour "ultradian" rhythms weaken significantly. New research shows aging decouples physical activity from core body temperature while triggering immune gene activation and neuronal loss inside the brain's master clock.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Aging, brain research, circadian rhythm, movement, neurobiology, temperature, ultradian rhythm, University of Tsukuba

title: Scent and Memory: Why Novelty Boosts Recall in Older Adults
summary: Can diffusing lavender really sharpen your memory? A new study reveals that scent alone doesn't boost recall, unless older adults experience it as a novel sensory cue at the very beginning of learning.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Aging, brain research, Memory, neurobiology, olfaction, UCLA

title: How ADHD Shapes Breathing and Time Perception
summary: ADHD reaches far beyond inattention and hyperactivity. New studies reveal that the condition alters breathing patterns, triggers chronic time pressure, lowers regional brain iron in youth, and influences problem drinking in young adults.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, ADHD, breathing, brian research, neurobiology, SfN, time perception

title: How Lead Exposure Erodes Long-Term Memory
summary: How does environmental lead exposure erode memory? Researchers found lead disrupts oxidation-reduction balance inside neuronal mitochondria, shutting down the new protein synthesis required to lock in long-term memories.
category: Featured, Genetics, Neuroscience, brain research, China Medical University, environmental neuroscience, lead exposure, Memory, mitochondria, neurobiology

title: Why Viruses Make You Sneeze: COVID Proteins Directly Hijack Sensory Nerves
summary: Why do colds, flu, and COVID make us sneeze, cough, and ache? Researchers found the SARS-CoV-2 enzymes directly hijack pain-sensing airway nerves via the "wasabi receptor" (TRPA1), triggering symptoms independently of immune inflammation.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, COVID-19, neurobiology, sensory neuroscience, UC Berkeley

title: Genetic Switch Helped Evolve the Large Primate Brain
summary: How did the human brain evolve to be so large and complex? Researchers discovered a primate-specific DNA regulatory switch controlling the shared DACH1 gene, boosting specialized basal radial glia stem cells that build the cerebral cortex without needing new genes.
category: Events, Genetics, Neuroscience, brain evolution, brain research, evolution, evolutionary neuroscience, neurobiology

title: CRISPR Enhancer Editing Rescues Autism Brain Organoids
summary: Rather than cutting DNA, scientists used precision CRISPR activation aimed at natural gene "dials" to boost healthy copies of CHD8 and SCN2A in human brain organoids, restoring normal tissue growth and neuronal firing exclusively in mutated cells.
category: Autism, Featured, Genetics, Neuroscience, ASD, brain development, brain research, developmental neuroscience, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, UCLA

title: Mapping the Brain’s Energy Budget: How ATP Fuels Thought
summary: How much energy does a single thought cost? The study will map the brain's metabolic budget across scales, solving why active neurons burn sugar rapidly and how brain cells survive oxygen loss.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, ATP, Boston University, brain research, cognition, neurobiology

title: Hidden Body Map in Brain Explains Complex Coordination
summary: How do you effortlessly coordinate your hand, arm, head, and lips to sip soup? Columbia neuroscientists discovered a previously hidden full-body map inside the brain's secondary motor cortex (M2), found within its resting-state neural chatter, that orchestrates complex multi-limb actions.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, body map, brain research, coordination, movement, neurobiology, Zuckerman Institute

title: Irregular Sleep Schedules Tied to Depression & Loneliness
summary: When you sleep matters just as much as how long you sleep. Analyzing five months of smart-ring data from 23,000 adults, researchers found that irregular daily sleep-wake schedules weaken circadian alignment and correspond with severe depression, anxiety, and loneliness.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, anxiety, brain research, circadian rhythm, depression, loneliness, mental health, neurobiology, Sleep, sleep-wake cycle, UCSF

title: 3D Genome Atlas Reveals Early Roots of Schizophrenia
summary: How does the human brain wire its reward and motor centers before birth? Using 3D genome sequencing across nearly 287,000 brain cells, UCLA scientists mapped the developing basal ganglia from mid-pregnancy to infancy, pinpointing how spiny projection neurons carry early genetic risk for schizophrenia.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain development, brain mapping, brain research, developmental neuroscience, mental health, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, Schizophrenia, UCLA
